items.exemplar:
A. The signers intended to create a legitimate civil government even though they had landed outside the bounds of their Virginia charter. By 'covenant and combine ourselves together into a civil Body Politick,' they agreed to make and obey laws for the colony's 'better Ordering and Preservation.'

B. One reason English colonies succeeded was their early practice of self-government. Virginia's House of Burgesses (1619) gave settlers a voice in their affairs, drawing more migrants and defusing conflict with authority.

C. The French enjoyed the advantage of strong Native alliances. Because their fur-trade empire depended on Native hunters and middlemen, the French built partnerships rather than seizing farmland, sparing them the costly wars that drained English colonies.
parts: A. Briefly explain what the signers of the Mayflower Compact intended to accomplish.
B. Briefly explain ONE reason English colonies in the New World proved successful.
C. Briefly explain ONE advantage enjoyed by the rival French colonies.
items.stimulus:
"We, whose names are underwritten, the Loyal Subjects of our dread Sovereign Lord King James... Having undertaken for the Glory of God, and Advancement of the Christian Faith, and the Honour of our King and Country, a Voyage to plant the first Colony in the northern Parts of Virginia; Do by these Presents, solemnly and mutually, in the Presence of God and one another, covenant and combine ourselves together into a civil Body Politick, for our better Ordering and Preservation..."
—Mayflower Compact, 1620
